newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says stance on forex markets unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says stance on forex markets unchanged.

text.p: Japan's stance on the foreign exchange markets remains unchanged, Haruhiko Kuroda, director general of the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) international bureau told reporters on Wednesday.
Asked whether Japan needs to keep a close watch over the current weakness of the yen against the dollar, Kuroda said, "Our basic stance remains unchanged." He did not elaborate further.
Asked whether the market was reflecting economic fundamentals, he said: "We will keep a careful watch over market movements, but there is nothing we need to say in particular at the moment."

Asked about the rise in Japan's trade surplus, as shown in the 126 percent year-on-year rise in the customs-cleared trade surplus in the first 20 days of July, Kuroda said he did not think the trend in the surplus had changed, but added Japan will keep a close watch over trade movements.
